Dear Dr. Clayton,
Re: Ms. Tracy Bowen

DOB 22/07/1988

Upon her request, I am writing to refer Ms. Bowen, a 32-year-old married woman, who has
features suggestive of polycystic ovarian syndrome. Your expert assessment and further
management would be highly appreciated.

Ms. Bowen had experienced painful, infrequent and irregular menstruation since her menarche,
for which she was receiving oral contraceptive pills and analgesics.

On 21/09/2005, Ms. Bowen presented at my clinic with deep, inflamed nodules and cystic acne
spread on her face and different body parts. Accordingly, she was prescribed systemic and local
antibiotics. However, her acne condition had continued to worsen over the following two
months, therefore, she was referred to a dermatologist.

Today, Ms. Bowen reported that she had stopped taking the oral contraceptive pills; however,
she was finding difficulty in getting pregnant. Additionally, she complained of amenorrhea,
depression and weight gain. On examination, her BMI was 28 and hirsutism was observed. Her
labarotory investigations revealed low levels of vitamin D and FSH hormone. However, there was
an increased in oral glucose tolerance test and free androgen index. Besides that, a significantly
elevated prolactin level was detected. Thus, she was prescribed Climen 10 mg four times daily,
and a pelvic ultrasound was ordered.

Kindly find an attached copy of her test results for your valuable review.

Should you have any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely
Doctor
